case_name: Prakash Chandra Mehta v Commissioner and Secretary, Government of Kerala and Others
respondent: Commissioner and Secretary, Government of Kerala
facts: One allegedly Venilal D. Mehta is the father. Miss Pragna Mehta is the daughter and Bharat Mehta is the son. They all have been detained under the Provisions of Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'), by virtue of an order dated 19th June, 1984.

The father and daughter Venilal D. Mehta and Pragna Mehta were arrested by the officers of the Central Excise and Customs, Cochin on all accusation of having in their possession 60 gold biscuits alleged to be of foreign origin.
After their arrest, the father and his daughter were taken to the office of the Central Excise and Customs, Cochin where statements were made on their behalf.
It is alleged that such statements were obtained by use of third degree method, molestation of the daughter, threat and intimidation.
The father, Venilal D. Mehta put his signature in English as 'Balvant Shah'.
After the said statement, the father and the daughter were taken to the Hotel Dwarka where they were kept in separate rooms under the guard of the officers.

On 2nd May, 1984, he was informed by his brother from Bombay that his father Venilal Mehta and his sister Pragna Mehta had been arrested and upon hearing that he left for Bombay and arrived in Bombay by the evening flight.
issues: Whether the detention of the petitioners under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 is valid or not.
Whether the statements made by the petitioners were obtained voluntarily or not.
petitioner_arguments: The father and daughter told the officers concerned that the correct name of the father was Venilal Mehta.
The father does not understand, read or speak or write English but he can only sign his name in English.
The statements made by the petitioners were obtained by use of third degree method, molestation of the daughter, threat and intimidation.
respondent_arguments: There was no provision for home cooked food and there was no solitary confinement, that interviews, and all outgoing and incoming letters are required to be censored and no special restrictions have been imposed upon her.
holding: The exercise of the power of preventive detention must be strictly within the safeguards provided. The purpose of exercise of all such powers by the Government must be to promote common well-being and must be to sub-serve the common good.
These petitions fail and are accordingly dismissed.
